Write a values file

Source: R/values.R
weft_values_write.Rd

weft_values_write() writes the values it is given to a JSON file in the form of a weft-values block (schema 1), for a document to read with a weft-values block that names the file (rules 2.13.10, 3.8.5). It works outside a knit, and in a targets pipeline. In a knitr document R reads a named value itself, so a values file is for a document that runs no R, or for a pipeline that computes the values elsewhere.

Usage

weft_values_write(path, ...)

Arguments

path

The file to write. A relative path is relative to the working directory.

...

Named values, or names of variables, as above. An argument may be a call of claim().

Value

path, invisibly.

Details

Each argument after path writes one name: weft_values_write(f, depth = mean(d$depth)), or weft_values_write(f, depth, n_sites) for variables of the same names. A name is ASCII letters, digits, _ and ., starting with a letter or _, at most 64 characters. An argument that is a call of claim() is captured: its checks are run and recorded with the value, nothing is stopped, and each check counts where the name is used.

A bool, a whole or decimal number, a string, a factor, a Date, an integer64 or an atomic vector of these (up to 10000 elements) is written with its kind. NA, NaN, Inf and NULL are written as missing. A value with units is refused, and any other object (a data frame, a list, a POSIXct, a function) is written as an error that is reported where the name is used.

The file is written atomically, as UTF-8 with \\n line ends. Nothing is written when an argument is refused, and the old file stays.

Examples

f <- tempfile(fileext = ".json")
weft_values_write(f, n = 12L, site = "north")
cat(readLines(f), sep = "\n")
#> {"weft":1,"lang":"r","run":null,"at":1795795700,"values":{"n":{"t":"int","v":"12"},"site":{"t":"string","v":"north"}}}
